Hi Sam — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and the handful of clarifying questions we promised to follow up on.

Call recap (high level)
- Goal: pilot Redwood inference for critical customer-facing fraud models (low-latency scoring).
- Primary constraint: strict data isolation and no egress of raw customer data off FinServe-controlled infrastructure unless contractually permitted.
- Two deployment models in scope: Dedicated (Redwood-managed GPUs in our infra) vs Private (customer VPC or on-prem).

Questions we had for you
1) Can you confirm whether \"no egress\" means: a) no network egress to Redwood's control plane at all, or b) allowed control-plane signals with explicit egress rules and encrypted payloads?
2) Is customer-managed KMS / HSM a hard requirement for key custody? Or is using our KMS with attestations acceptable for the pilot?
3) If we proposed a Private VPC deployment (Redwood control plane in FinServe VPC) — would FinServe allow our collector/monitoring agents to communicate to a monitoring endpoint inside your DMZ, or must observability be entirely push-only to FinServe-owned destinations?

Next steps I propose
- I'll attach a short architecture sketch for Private VPC and a checklist for on-prem (attached: redwood-private-arch.pdf).
- If you confirm answers to Q1–Q3, we can scope an SRE call (solutions eng + FinServe infra) to validate networking and KMS steps.
- Separately, please send your security questionnaire and I'll have our trust team start filling it (if you already have one, attach it and I'll route).

Would love confirmation on the three bullets above. Happy to hop on another 30m if useful.

Thanks,

Karthik — great summary, thank you. Short answers below.

Q1: No egress means no flow of raw PII or transaction data outside FinServe-managed networks. We can allow out-of-band control-plane signals (status, health) only if they are strictly metadata (no payload) and routed via our approved endpoints.
Q2: Customer-managed KMS is required for the pilot. We need key custody in our HSM and key rotation control.
Q3: Observability must be push-only to FinServe-owned collectors. We will not permit Redwood-managed monitoring endpoints inside our DMZ.

Given the above, we are inclined toward Private VPC with customer-managed KMS or an on-prem deployment. Dedicated (Redwood-managed) is out unless you can guarantee no data leaves our environment (which would need a contract + design that I doubt is feasible for this pilot).

I attached FinServe's security questionnaire — please have your trust team start it. Also include a one-pager that explains what the Private VPC networking topology looks like (peering, NAT/eip rules), and a note about latency expectations for a FinServe region.

Karthik / Marissa — quick technical note:

Private VPC option (our recommendation for this constraint)
- Feasibility: Yes. We can deploy Redwood Private control plane into a customer VPC or run the control plane remotely but with all data ingress/egress constrained by customer-managed gateways.
- KMS/HSM: We support customer-managed encryption keys via external KMS endpoints (KMIP-like) or by bringing-your-own-key with a remote HSM integration. For the pilot, the simplest path is TLS-mutual auth to FinServe KMS endpoints; integration time ~1–2 weeks for basic testing, 3–4 weeks for hardened production config and rotation testing.
- Observability: We can push logs/metrics to FinServe collectors only (push-only). We will need a list of collector endpoints and a short-lived token exchange pattern.
- Network: VPC peering + route tables + SGs; avoid public NAT for data paths. We'll need ephemeral egress for control-plane mating (metadata only) — but this can be disabled if FinServe insists.

On-prem option
- Feasibility: Also supported but higher friction. On-prem requires image packaging, installer runbook, and on-site validation. Estimate 4–6 weeks prep + a 1–2 week on-site validation window.

Tradeoffs
- Private VPC: faster to stand up, easier for us to manage and patch, still gives FinServe network controls and isolation.
- On-prem: maximal control for FinServe but longer time-to-market and higher operational burden on FinServe.

I'll draft a concise architecture diagram and a checklist (I can use Karthik's redwood-private-arch.pdf as a base) — ping me if you want a call with our SRE next week.

Cheers,
